title: Can AI turn a pile of fund PDFs into one family office report?
description: From capital call notices and fund PDFs to the family's quarterly report: what AI reads and matches, why private values lag, and who signs off.
verdict: The quarterly report is the sorest job: 73% of 155 North American family offices call investment reporting too manual.[^1][^12]
The pile behind it grows: the average private markets investment sends 13 documents a year, in waves.[^49][^50]
AI reads each notice and statement and matches it to the books; a person checks each figure against its page.[^55][^57]
Private-fund values arrive one to four months late, so print the lag on the report.[^5][^6]
Let AI draft the commentary, never sign it: drafts can get every number right and invent causes.[^7][^8]

summary: AI for family office reporting turns the quarter's fund statements, notices and custodian files into one view across the family's entities.[^11][^49] People check each figure and the drafted commentary.[^12][^7] Private-fund values make or break it: they arrive months late.[^5][^13]

answers.human-role: The controller clears every break and the COO signs off the report, because AI drafts can state every number right and still add causes nobody supplied.[^7][^3]
answers.team-after: Your team moves from keying and matching to clearing breaks, checking private-fund values and building the views the family asks for.[^3][^9]
answers.example: An illustrative six-person office feeds in custodian files, bank data and fund statements, and gets back a draft look-through balance sheet, a break list and labelled fund values.[^11][^14]
answers.table-3: Published prices run from $250 a year for Kubera Essentials to $35,899 a year for FundCount's single family office plan, before fees.[^15][^16] Masttro publishes no price and quotes each deal.[^17]
answers.table-4: Private-fund reports are due within 60 days after quarter end under Institutional Limited Partners Association (ILPA) guidance, and later for funds of funds.[^6]
answers.table-5: Surveys agree reporting is the office's sorest spot: 73% of North American family offices call it too manual, while 47% of offices use third-party reporting software.[^1][^10]
answers.recipes: Small offices should run reporting on one platform, and offices with many private funds should add an AI check layer that reads statements and sorts breaks.[^18][^9]
answers.own-data: Public pensions write the lag down: 8 of 11 plans we read state a private-value lag, and 4 say how values are brought current, by our count.[^19][^20]
answers.rules: Few rules govern a single family office's own report: an office serving only family is not an investment adviser, though Form 13F filing can still apply.[^21][^22]
answers.benchmark: Run AI beside today's process for two quarter ends on one custodian and five private funds, then count breaks caught, causes invented and days saved.[^23][^7]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI family office reporting goes wrong when stale fund values go unlabelled, drafts invent causes, retrieval misses the source page, or ownership is mapped wrong.[^24][^7][^25][^11]
answers.buy-or-build: Buy the aggregation platform, because custodian feeds number in the hundreds, and build only the checks and views your family needs.[^17][^9]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when the books are simple, keying fund statements is the bottleneck, security comes first, or the ledger is not reconciled yet.[^15][^26]
answers.table-1: Each quarter brings capital call and distribution notices, capital account statements and K-1s.[^59][^51] AI pulls a handful of fields from each, and a person checks each one against its page.[^57]
answers.table-2: The Institutional Limited Partners Association (ILPA) reporting template puts each fund's fees, expenses and chargebacks in one layout from Q1 2026, so every fund reads the same way.[^60]

humanRole: Controller: clears each break the platform or AI flags.[^3][^14] Black Diamond says 99.5% of accounts complete automatically, yet its brief says exceptions are still researched and adjusted by hand.[^3]
Investment operations analyst: checks each extracted figure and private-fund value against the general partner (GP) statement it came from, with the document attached.[^14][^27]
COO: sets the AI policy, the approved tools and who sees which data.[^9] Two-factor sign-in among offices fell from 92% to 83%, so check it before any tool reads custodian data.[^1]
Controller and COO: read every AI-written sentence before the principal sees it.[^7][^8] BNY finds judgment and oversight in family offices remain largely human-led.[^12]
teamAfter: Controllers move from keying statements to clearing the breaks the match leaves.[^3][^13]
Analysts check the private-fund line: the statement date, the roll-forward for cash flows and the label.[^5][^27]
Some offices rely on one or two platform power users; they build the views the family asks for.[^9] Meeting family members' needs is the top challenge for 54% of offices.[^18]
Where AI changed tasks, 66% of US firms use it only to help staff, and AI-related employment fell at only 2% of AI-using firms.[^28]

example.input: Illustrative: a six-person office with 30 entities (trusts, LLCs and a foundation), four custodians, two banks and 45 private funds. It is mid-May, and the March quarter report is due. Custodian files, bank feeds and 45 general partner statements, most still dated 31 December.
example.output: A draft balance sheet by entity, plus a look-through of the principal's share with no holding counted twice. A break list that flags a share-class code change as a closed and a new position. Fund lines labelled "31 Dec value, rolled forward for first-quarter cash flows", and draft commentary with each stated cause flagged for the controller.

recipes.name: 1. Small office: one platform, people check
recipes.when: Offices with six people or fewer, which are 63% of offices in Citi's survey.[^18] Lean on the platform's feeds, since offices average fewer than one IT professional.[^31]
flow: COO: pick one platform and map every entity and ownership percentage into it
Controller: connect custodian and bank feeds
Analyst: enter each GP statement with the document attached
Platform AI: match positions and draft the commentary
Controller: clear each break and strike any cause the inputs don't support
COO: label each private value with its statement date, then sign off
recipes.cost: Published prices run from $250 a year for Kubera Essentials to $35,899 a year for FundCount's single family office plan, before fees.[^15][^16]

recipes.name: 2. Office with many private funds: platform plus an AI check layer
recipes.when: Offices with several custodians and dozens of private funds, where statements are keyed by hand.[^13] The platform does the plumbing; you build the checks and the view.[^9]
flow: Controller: keep the platform as the book of record
AI: read each GP statement into fields, linked to its page
Analyst: approve each extracted value and roll it forward for cash flows
AI: sort breaks by cause, such as timing, data mismatch or a changed security code
Controller: clear the breaks and sign the reconciliation
AI: draft commentary from approved numbers only
COO: read every sentence, strike unsupported causes and release the report
recipes.cost: Asora quotes $15,600 a year at one net worth tier, plus $3,900 onboarding and $3,600 a year per 20 alternative holdings.[^29] Median IT spend among offices is U.S. $100,000.[^1]

ownData.title: How do public pension plans label the private-markets lag?
ownData.intro: On 28 Nov 2026 we read how 11 US public pension plans word the lag on private-market values in their own reports.[^19][^32] We copied each plan's wording and marked whether it says how values are brought current.[^33][^34]
headers: Says how values are brought current?
rows: New York State Common Retirement Fund
Private equity, real estate and real assets "reported on a three-month lag"[^19]
Private asset performance "reported with a quarter lag"[^32]
Private fund values "reported on a quarter lag"[^33]
Yes: adjusted "to bring the lagged valuations current"[^33]
June valuations used for the quarter to September[^34]
"a one quarter lag inherent in private equity valuations"[^35]
Private equity and its benchmark "lagged one calendar quarter"[^36]
Returns reported "with a one-quarter lag for PE"[^37]
Private equity "reported on a three-month lag"[^38]
Benchmarks "lagged one quarter"; no valuation lag stated[^39]
"Benchmark returns are reported on a one-quarter lag"[^40]
"subject to reporting lags"; no length given[^20]
ownData.note: Method: we read each plan's annual report, program review or a state oversight paper on 28 Nov 2026 and copied the wording. By our count, 8 state a valuation lag, 2 state only a benchmark lag, and Florida gives no length. Limits: 11 plans, not every plan; Oregon and Virginia come from state papers; we compared wording, not returns.

rules.name: Family office rule, 17 CFR 275.202(a)(11)(G)-1
rules.what: An office is not an investment adviser under the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rule if it serves only family and is family-owned.[^21] It must also not hold itself out to the public.[^21] Its internal report is then not an adviser's client communication; a registered multi-family office's report is.

rules.name: SEC Form 13F
rules.what: A manager with investment discretion over $100 million or more in 13(f) securities files Form 13F each quarter.[^22] The filing is due within 45 days after quarter end, even for an office exempt from adviser rules.[^22]

rules.name: NIST AI 600-1, Generative AI Profile
rules.what: NIST names confabulation, confident but false content, as a risk to manage.[^8] Use it as the frame for the office's written AI policy and its review step.

howToTest: Record today's numbers for one quarter: days from quarter end to final report, reconciliation hours and open breaks. In a FundCount-sponsored survey of 27 family office professionals, time to produce final reports was the most-used KPI (key performance indicator).[^23]
Pick one custodian and five private funds as the pilot; keep everything else on today's process.
Run the AI match beside today's reconciliation for two quarter ends, and count breaks caught, missed and raised in error.
Sort each break by cause: timing, data mismatch, or a changed security code.[^4][^14]
Test the retrieval, not just the model: one benchmark's accuracy fell to 0.2% when the model lacked the right pages.[^25]
Check the words as well as the numbers: mark every cause or judgment the draft adds that no input supports.[^7]
Price the lift: hours saved times loaded cost, plus days cut from quarter end to the report the family reads.
watchOuts: Stale private values: private equity values typically arrive 45 to 75 days after quarter end.[^24] Print each fund line's statement date and roll-forward, as pension plans do.[^19][^5]
Right numbers, wrong story: AI drafts add causes no one supplied, and AI readers took an invented cause as the reason in 99% of texts.[^7] Have the controller strike every unsupported cause.[^7]
Retrieval misses: GPT-4-Turbo with retrieval answered wrong or refused on 81% of FinanceBench questions.[^41] In another benchmark, retrieval caused 66.5% of failures.[^25]

Long fund documents drop records: one model's accuracy fell from 87.9% on short files to 27.9% on long ones, mostly from records it missed.[^54] Count rows, not only fields, on K-1 footnote packages.[^52]
Feeds are not the whole picture: about 40% of family offices still worry about spreadsheets and manual aggregation.[^30] In some offices, private-markets data sits outside the platform.[^9]

Double counting across entities: map each entity's ownership share and multiply down the chain.[^11] A FundCount-sponsored survey of 44 family offices ranked missing look-through reporting among its main system weaknesses.[^42]

faq.q: Why does our quarterly report take weeks?
faq.a: Private-fund statements arrive late by design: ILPA guidance gives direct funds 60 days after quarter end, and funds of funds 120.[^6] Keying them by hand adds the rest.[^13]

faq.q: Can AI read our capital account statements and K-1s?
faq.a: Yes, for the first pass: reporting platforms and alternatives services extract the fields, and a person validates them.[^57][^55] On long files one model's accuracy fell from 87.9% to 27.9%, so count rows as well as fields.[^54]

faq.q: What should we pull from each capital call notice?
faq.a: Pull the fund, date, net amount, its fee and investment lines and the wire instructions, then match the cash to the notice.[^59][^56] A second person confirms any changed wire instructions by phone.[^53]

faq.q: Can AI collect our LP reporting from every fund portal?
faq.a: Yes, by the vendors' own account: Arch and Canoe say they collect capital calls, statements and K-1s from general partner portals and inboxes.[^56][^58] Check each tool's portal list against your funds before you buy.[^49]

faq.q: Does this cover private equity portfolio monitoring?
faq.a: Yes, from the family's side: the same statements and notices track each fund's value, cash flows and unfunded commitment quarter by quarter.[^61][^5] Values lag one to four months, so label each with its statement date.[^5]

faq.q: Can AI reconcile custodian feeds against our ledger and flag breaks?
faq.a: Yes, but platforms already match most accounts, so AI pays on sorting the breaks.[^3] Black Diamond says 99.5% of accounts complete automatically, yet its brief says exceptions are still researched and adjusted by hand.[^3]

faq.q: Can we say on the report that private values are stale?
faq.a: Yes, and large investors already do: New York's pension fund says private equity is reported on a three-month lag, adjusted by cash flows.[^19]

faq.q: Who signs off before the family sees the report?
faq.a: The COO signs off after the controller has read every AI-written sentence, because drafts can state every number right and still add causes.[^7][^9]

faq.q: What does the family want to see first?
faq.a: The principal wants net worth, liquidity and major changes in one view, says Masttro, a reporting vendor.[^43] Meeting family members’ needs is the top challenge for 54% of offices.[^18]

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy the aggregation and accounting platform: Simple’s 2026 report sums the pattern up as buy the plumbing, build the view.[^9] Vendors typically quote 2 to 4 months to implement.[^9] Across US enterprise AI decision-makers, 76% of AI use cases are now bought rather than built.[^44]
buyVsBuild.build: Build the check layer and the views on top, because your entity map, labels and review rules are your own.[^9][^11] For organizations, partnered builds reached deployment about 67% of the time, against about 33% for internal builds.[^45]

pickElse: Small office with simple books: a household tool such as Kubera Essentials, at $250 a year for 2 portfolios and 2 users, may be enough.[^15]
Keying fund statements is the bottleneck: start with document capture, as in our AI document processing guide.[^46][^29]
Security comes first: cybersecurity is now the top near-term concern for 59% of offices, up from 16%.[^26] Fix sign-in and payment controls before adding tools.[^1]
The ledger isn't reconciled yet: fix the close first, with our multi-entity close and reconciliation guides.[^47][^48]

sources.what: Survey of 44 family offices plus 20 interviews. A lack of consolidated or look-through reporting across entities and investments was among the main system weaknesses; look-through reporting is "one of the main challenges family offices face". Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Masttro, family office reporting (vendor)
sources.what: Vendor explainer: "A principal wants to see net worth, liquidity and major changes without going through a training session." Its list of seven core reports starts with consolidated net worth. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Menlo Ventures, 2025 State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
sources.what: Survey of 495 US enterprise AI decision-makers: 76% of AI use cases are purchased rather than built, up from 53% in 2024. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: MIT NANDA, The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025 (Jul 2025)
sources.what: MIT no longer hosts the report (its link now opens the NANDA project page, checked 26 Nov 2026); copy hosted by MLQ.ai. Sample: 52 organizations interviewed, survey of 153 leaders, and 300+ public AI initiatives reviewed. $30-40 billion of enterprise GenAI investment; 95% of organizations are getting zero return; just 5% of integrated AI pilots extract millions in value. Task-specific tools: 60% of organizations evaluated them, 20% piloted, 5% reached production. Over 80% of organizations explored or piloted ChatGPT or Copilot, and nearly 40% report deployment. External partnerships with customized tools reached deployment about 67% of the time vs about 33% for internal builds: 2x as likely, twice the success rate. Only 40% of companies purchased an official LLM subscription; workers at over 90% of companies surveyed use personal AI tools for work. For mission-critical work, 90% of users prefer humans. Enterprises, defined as firms with over $100 million in annual revenue, lead in pilot count but report the lowest pilot-to-scale conversion. Read 26 Nov 2026.

sources.what: Zavient guide to AI that reads financial documents, with our own extraction benchmark.

sources.name: Zavient, Can AI speed up consolidated financial reporting across add-ons?
sources.what: Zavient guide to closing and consolidating the books across many entities.

sources.name: Arch, The Hidden Costs of Alts: Your Inbox Is About to Grow 5x (vendor platform data)
sources.what: Vendor platform data, Sep 2025 to Aug 2026, covering a sample of 12,800 fund managers: the average private markets investment sends 13 documents a year; the top decile sends 25 or more. Documents arrive in waves after each quarter end, and "over half of all K-1s arrive in just three months". Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Canoe Intelligence, The Future-Ready Family Office, 18 Mar 2026 (vendor poll)
sources.what: Poll of 70+ family offices at a conference, run by a vendor. Biggest issue in processing alternatives documents: collection, 36% of family offices voting; extracting key metrics from documents 27%; data accuracy and consistency 9%. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: IRS, 2025 Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)
sources.what: The partner's K-1 form: Part I (items A-D), Part II (items E-N, including item L, the partner's capital account analysis: beginning capital account, capital contributed during the year, current year net income (loss), other increase (decrease), withdrawals and distributions, ending capital account) and Part III (boxes 1-23). By our count, 47 items and boxes. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: IRS, 2025 Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)
sources.what: The List of Codes for boxes 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19 and 20. By our count, 173 active codes, leaving out codes reserved for future use: box 11 has 18, box 13 has 29, box 14 has 3, box 15 has 55, box 17 has 6, box 18 has 3, box 19 has 6 and box 20 has 53. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: FBI, Business Email Compromise
sources.what: Advises to verify any change in account number or payment procedures with the person making the request, and to look up the phone number yourself rather than use one in the email. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: ExtractBench, arXiv 2607.29677v2 (by LlamaIndex, a vendor)
sources.what: Vendor-authored benchmark of 370 documents, including K-1, W-2 and 1040 tax forms. Best overall F1 95.6% (LlamaExtract Agentic Plus, 8.1 cents a page); Codex GPT-5.5 93.6% at 27.8 cents a page. Gemini 3.5 Flash scored 87.9% on short documents and 27.9% on long ones; on long documents its recall was 26.5 against precision of 83.7, so it missed records. Commercial vision-language models return no source evidence; best word-level grounding F1 46.4%, page-level 84.9%. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: RSM US, Strategic AI readiness in the family office
sources.what: Most AI features in family office systems are narrow, such as extracting values from capital call notices. AI is less about agents replacing staff and more about staff configuring and overseeing AI tools. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Arch, Family offices (vendor)
sources.what: Vendor claims: 700+ customers, 50,000+ funds and $600B+ supported. Collects documents from GP portals, extracts data with human-in-the-loop review and 200+ validation checks, chases late K-1s, checks wire instructions against past calls and checks the EIN. No price on the page. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Addepar, Alts Data Management (vendor)
sources.what: Vendor page: AI extraction of alternative investment documents with human validation, inside Addepar. No price on the page. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Canoe Intelligence (vendor)
sources.what: Vendor page: connects to GP portals and inboxes and extracts capital calls, distributions and capital account statements (PCAPs). No price on the page. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Masttro, Capital call processing for family offices (vendor)
sources.what: Vendor claims: family offices hold dozens or even hundreds of fund positions, and alternatives are about 45% of the portfolio. Masttro Alternatives AI flags mismatches and matches cash to calls within a three-day window. No price on the page. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: ILPA, ILPA Releases Updated Reporting Template and New Performance Template for Industry Adoption, 22 Jan 2025
sources.what: The updated Reporting Template breaks out internal chargebacks and gives more granular partnership expenses; the new Performance Template standardizes IRR and TVPI/MOIC, gross and net, with and without the impact of fund-level subscription facilities. "The new templates should be implemented beginning Q1 of 2026." Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: ILPA, Capital Call & Distribution Template Suggested Guidance 2025
sources.what: The Capital Call & Distribution Template v2.0, released September 2025, replaces the 2011 template: Fund-level and LP-level information, a Transactions Table with each transaction's impact on the LP unfunded commitment, and supplemental management fee and carry calculations. First delivery is expected in Q1 2027. The template was not designed for verifying any of the GP's calculations. Read 28 Nov 2026.

offer.heading: Want one quarterly report the family can trust? Get a free diagnostic
offer.body: Bring your entity map, your custodians and last quarter's report. In 30 minutes you leave with the first step, a before-and-after measure and where the lag label goes. You get it in writing, with no sales pitch.

reviews.notes: Clear on who clears breaks and who signs off, and the lag label is copyable. Bottom-line bullet on reconciliation read vaguely ("AI pays on the breaks"); reworded to say AI earns its keep sorting the breaks staff still research.
Test plan is runnable on one quarter. The benchmark answer said "a few funds" while the steps say five; aligned both to one custodian and five private funds.
Bottom line answers the question in five bullets; prices and survey samples are labelled. Confabulation is explained in plain words. No change.

Read as the controller and investment operations lead. Fund-timing table and roll-forward wording match how the office works; the share-class break example is realistic. Dropped the document-processing sibling link, which will not publish; fund statement capture points to the live document processing guide. No other change.
Answers whether the family can trust one report and what it costs in outside software, with labelled vendor prices. Offer is concrete. No change; no Zavient price, by decision.
